The 130th Boston Marathon is scheduled for Monday, April 20, 2026, marking the world's oldest annual marathon, featuring 30,000+ runners traversing a 26.2-mile course from Hopkinton to Boston’s Boylston Street. Key highlights include challenging landmarks like Heartbreak Hill, a six-wave start, and extensive city-wide road closures. Key Details for 2026 Date: Monday, April 20, 2026 (Patriots' Day). Start Times: Elite Wheelchair begins at 9:02 a.m., Pro Women at 9:45 a.m., and Pro Men at 9:37 a.m. The rolling start for other waves runs from 10:00 a.m. to 11:21 a.m.. Field Size: 24,362 qualifiers were accepted to start, with registration often reaching record-fast qualifying times. Course: Starts in Hopkinton, moving through towns like Ashland, Framingham, Natick, Wellesley, and Newton before ending in Copley Square. Spectator Info: The city advises against driving near the finish line due to closures, suggesting parking in garages like 100 Clarendon, Copley Place, or the Boston Common Garage. 100 Clarendon Copley Place Boston Common Garage Tracking: Runners can be tracked via the official B.A.A. Racing App. B.A.A. Racing App Important Notes for Participants Qualification: Standards are strict, with 2026 seeing some of the fastest cut-off times, often requiring runners to be minutes faster than their standard. Charity/Travel: Charity runners or those booking travel packages can use organizations like Marathon Tours & Travel for access to the event, which may include unique, high-value entry packages. Marathon Tours & Travel Road Closures: Major roads along the route (Route 135 and Route 16) will be closed, particularly in Newton and Boston. The race is famous for its festive atmosphere, culminating in a 600-meter straightaway on Boylston Street.
